findings.issue: sprint-AJ1 adds session_id to TeamMemberHeartbeatResponse as a passive field (derive-driven serde only, no behavioral spec). sprint-AJ5 then specifies that the response carries 'post-update read, not the value from the request.' This is a cross-sprint contradiction in ownership: AJ.1 defines the struct's shape, AJ.5 retroactively assigns its semantics. The response-value contract must be stated in AJ.1 where the field is introduced, not discovered later in AJ.5.
findings.required_correction: Move the response semantics sentence ('echoes the session_id that is now cached after the update, not the request value') into sprint-AJ1.md under Interfaces or Deliverables. AJ.5 may reference it but must not be the first place it appears.

findings.issue: TeamMemberHeartbeatRequest.pid is u32 (required, always present), while WriteRequest.pid and ReadQuery.pid are Option<u32> (optional, may be None). The non-overwrite rule says None does not overwrite — but heartbeat ALWAYS carries a pid. This means every heartbeat unconditionally overwrites any pid previously set by a CLI dispatch. The plan is silent on whether this asymmetry is intentional or accidental. If intentional, it needs an explicit design rule. If accidental, heartbeat.pid should also be Option<u32>.
findings.required_correction: Add a 'Pid Overwrite Policy' subsection to plan-phase-aj.md Design Rules: explicitly state that heartbeat.pid always overwrites cached pid (because heartbeat is the canonical liveness authority), while CLI-supplied pid only sets when Some. Or change TeamMemberHeartbeatRequest.pid to Option<u32> to match the other paths.

findings.issue: Design rule states 'in-memory only, no SQLite persistence' as a constraint without a documented ADR justifying why. Several justifications are plausible (ephemeral by design, avoiding migration tax, performance), but none are written. A downstream developer who wants to persist session state will have no decision record to consult.
findings.required_correction: Add an AD-AJ-2 section (or extend AD-AJ-1) under phase-plan-aj.md with at minimum: (a) rationale for in-memory over SQLite, (b) what would trigger reconsideration, (c) migration path if persistence is added later.

findings.issue: sprint-AJ1 defines SessionId as a newtype wrapper but never justifies why a newtype over a plain String. Is this for type safety? Future validation? Serde guarantees? The choice is defensible but undocumented.
findings.required_correction: Add a one-paragraph justification to sprint-AJ1.md: why newtype, what invariants it enforces (or explicitly states it enforces none yet), and how it prevents conflation with other string-like identifiers in the codebase.

minor_wording.issue: sprint-AJ4 lists cached_session_id() as a new public accessor but never specifies its return type or error handling — only the method name.
minor_wording.suggested_cleanup: Add return type signature: pub fn cached_session_id(&self, team: &TeamName, member: &AgentName) -> Option<SessionId>

minor_wording.issue: Sprint AJ.5 says 'forwards session_id to the cache via the same non-overwrite write path used by touch_member' — ambiguous whether record_heartbeat calls touch_member internally, or duplicates the non-overwrite logic inline.
minor_wording.suggested_cleanup: Clarify: either 'record_heartbeat calls touch_member(identity, session_id, None) for session_id only' or 'record_heartbeat applies the same Some/None gating inline'.

minor_wording.issue: Sprint AJ.2 says parse failure yields None, but doesn't specify whether negative numbers, zero, or u32::MAX are valid. pid: 0 is a real PID on some systems. No validation rules documented.
minor_wording.suggested_cleanup: Add a note: 'zero and negative values are rejected (return None). Valid range is 1..=u32::MAX. If tighter platform validation is needed, it belongs in a later phase.'
